events.title: Start of the Mayan Long Count Calendar
events.description: According to the most widely accepted correlation (GMT), August 11, 3114 BCE marks the mythical starting date of the Mesoamerican Long Count calendar, used by the Maya to track vast spans of time. Note: the year is BCE, represented here as a positive number.
events.significance: This date became widely known when the Long Count cycle reached 13 b'ak'tuns in December 2012, sparking global attention to Maya astronomy and timekeeping.

events.title: First Prisoners Arrive at Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary
events.description: The first federal prisoners arrived at Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay after the Department of Justice converted the former military prison into a maximum-security federal penitentiary. Among its inmates over the years would be notorious criminals such as Al Capone.
events.significance: Alcatraz became one of the most famous prisons in the world, symbolizing the federal government's tough stance on crime during the Depression era.

events.title: Watts Riots Begin in Los Angeles
events.description: A traffic stop of Marquette Frye in the Watts neighborhood escalated into six days of civil unrest. The riots resulted in 34 deaths, over 1,000 injuries, nearly 4,000 arrests, and about $40 million in property damage.
events.significance: The riots exposed deep racial and economic inequality in American urban areas and shaped national debate on police relations, poverty, and civil rights in the mid-1960s.

events.title: Total Solar Eclipse Crosses Europe and Asia
events.description: A total solar eclipse passed across Europe, the Middle East, and South Asia, with the path of totality crossing Cornwall in the UK, northern France, Germany, Austria, Hungary, Romania, and beyond to India. It was observed by millions of people.
events.significance: It was one of the most widely viewed total solar eclipses in history, drawing enormous public interest in astronomy across densely populated regions.

events.title: Birth of Hip Hop at a Bronx Party
events.description: DJ Kool Herc hosted a back-to-school party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue in the Bronx, New York, where he extended instrumental break sections of records using two turntables, a technique that became foundational to hip hop music.
events.significance: The event is widely regarded as the birthplace of hip hop, which grew into one of the most influential global cultural and musical movements.
